events.title: Two vacancies, six months open
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Both identity engineering roles are still open. We have been covering with the people we have, and it is starting to show in what we can commit to.

events.title: The team is past sustainable load
events.from: {{pressedLeader}}
events.body: I need to be straight with you. {{PressedFunction}} is running above what my people can sustain and has been for a while. If you add anything else, something already committed will slip, and I would rather choose which.

events.title: Someone is thinking of leaving
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: One of the senior analysts has been approached and is considering it. They have not said so directly, which is how these things usually surface.

events.title: Your architecture lead went further than asked
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: While mapping dependencies I also pulled the firewall rule base. There are rules between the legacy estate and production that nobody can account for. I have documented them.

events.title: Two documents, two different answers
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: The architecture pack says the legacy estate is fully segregated from production. The firewall rule base says otherwise. Both are current documents.

events.title: Corvus returns a clean questionnaire
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body:
Corvus has returned the annual assurance questionnaire fully compliant, including enforced multi-factor authentication for all privileged access.

I would like to believe it. I have not tested it.

events.title: Corvus returns a clean questionnaire
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body:
Corvus has returned the annual assurance questionnaire fully compliant, including enforced multi-factor authentication for all privileged access.

Our own review found the opposite: their engineers' remote access accepts a password alone. I have asked them which of the two answers they would like to stand behind.

events.title: The questionnaire was wrong
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Corvus told us their privileged access enforces multi-factor authentication. I checked the remote access configuration this morning. It does not, and it never has.

events.title: What do we do about standing supplier access?
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: We now have it documented: fourteen permanent privileged accounts belonging to Corvus, no expiry, and nobody has reviewed them in years. Procurement will help if we give them something specific. Operations will resist anything that touches night cover.

events.title: People Cloud discloses an incident
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: Our HR provider has notified customers of unauthorised access to a support system. The notification is vague about scope and firm about there being no evidence of customer data access.

events.title: The logistics integration has write access
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: Lattice Logistics' integration account can write to and delete records in order management. The integration only ever needed to read them.

events.title: 6,283 critical vulnerabilities
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body:
The number people keep quoting at you is real. It is also close to meaningless: about a third sit on an isolated development cluster with no inbound routes and no real data.

Eleven of them are on internet-facing services. Those are the ones I would look at.

events.title: Remediation is the constraint, not detection
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Median time to remediate a critical finding on production is 94 days. We are very good at finding things. We are not resourced to fix them.

events.title: The last restore test was abandoned
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: I went looking for the last recovery test report. The test was abandoned after eleven hours and the report was never reissued. Fourteen months ago.

events.title: Backups share credentials with what they protect
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: The backup platform is administered with the same privileged accounts as the systems it backs up. An actor with production administration would be able to remove the recovery path and the systems together.

events.title: The incident response plan names someone who left
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: The plan names an incident commander who left in March. It has not been exercised in two years. If something happens tomorrow, we will be inventing the process while using it.

events.title: Publicly readable storage in production
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Two storage buckets in the production tenancy permit anonymous read. One contains application logs including session identifiers. They have been like this for at least seven months.

events.title: A peering link nobody remembers creating
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: There is a network peering link between the development and production cloud tenancies. It was created for a migration in 2023. The migration finished. The link did not go away.

events.title: Container workloads can read the customer store
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: Workloads on the shared cluster inherit a platform role with broad read access to production data stores. Any compromised workload becomes a data problem.

events.title: 412 service accounts, no owners
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: 412 non-human accounts. 78 have passwords older than five years. 31 hold privileged rights. Nobody owns them, which means nobody can safely remove them.

events.title: The MFA exception register
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: 214 accounts sit on the multi-factor exception register. Most were granted as temporary. The oldest is three years old. Nineteen of them are administrative.

events.title: Partner accounts live in the staff directory
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: Partner identities for the extranet are held in the same identity platform, and the same tenant, as employee accounts. A partner credential compromise starts from inside our identity boundary.

events.title: An access review failed
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: A sample access review on order management found nine leavers with active accounts and two accounts with rights nobody could explain. The reviewer had approved the previous round without reading it.

events.title: Closed-account data is being kept indefinitely
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: Records for closed accounts are retained indefinitely in the analytics estate, contrary to our published retention policy. I have been told this is a technical limitation. I do not believe that is the whole story.

events.title: Card data outside the payment environment
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: A discovery scan found unencrypted card data in two application log stores outside the defined payment environment. The regulated boundary is wider than the one we have been describing.

events.title: Nobody can say what is in the legacy data centre
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: Three asset lists disagree on how many systems remain in the legacy estate. The range is between 60 and 140. Two of them are in the backup schedule. We think.

events.title: A programme has stalled
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: {{BlockedProgramme}} has been blocked for at least a week: {{blocker}}. It is still moving, at a fraction of its pace, and will stay that way until somebody clears it. The Programmes screen says what that takes.

variants.title: Still blocked
variants.body: {{BlockedProgramme}} is stuck again: {{blocker}}. It crawls rather than stops, which is why nobody is shouting about it yet.

variants.title: Blocked, and nobody has cleared it
variants.body: {{blocker}} is holding up {{blockedProgramme}}. Every week it stays there is a week of the plan we do not get back.

events.title: A programme is on plan
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: We are on plan for once, and nothing is blocking us. The team would like that noticed before it is quietly absorbed into the next set of expectations.

events.title: Coverage has quietly gone backwards
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Endpoint coverage has slipped this quarter. Nothing broke. The estate simply grew faster than deployment did.

variants.title: Endpoint coverage has slipped again
variants.body: Endpoint coverage is down again this quarter. New machines are arriving faster than the agent is being installed on them, and nobody owns closing the gap.

variants.title: New laptops, no agent
variants.body: The latest batch of new laptops went out without the endpoint agent. They work perfectly well. We just cannot see what happens on them.

variants.title: The estate keeps outgrowing the tooling
variants.body: Coverage has drifted backwards again. Every quarter we lose a little to growth, and every quarter the fix is a project nobody has funded.

events.title: Two tools doing the same job
events.from: Nadia Farrell, Director of Procurement and Supplier Management
events.body: We were paying for two products that do broadly the same thing, bought by different teams eighteen months apart. I have cancelled the one fewer people use, and the £90k comes back to the cyber budget this year.

effectsOnReveal.note: A duplicate tool has been cancelled.

events.title: A new starter, and a reminder
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Our new identity engineer starts next week. They will take about two months to be useful, which is worth remembering before we commit them to anything.

events.title: An assumption is due for review
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: The assumptions you recorded behind decisions earlier this year are ageing. They may still hold. Somebody should check rather than hope.

variants.title: Your assumptions are getting older
variants.body: Some of what you recorded as true earlier in the year was true when you wrote it down. Whether it still is, nobody has checked.

variants.title: Worth checking what you assumed
variants.body: Decisions you took this year rest on assumptions you recorded at the time. The organisation has moved since, and an assumption does not tell you when it stops being true.

variants.title: Assumptions do not check themselves
variants.body: A reminder rather than a problem: the assumptions behind this year's decisions have not been looked at since you recorded them. The ones that matter most are the ones worth an enquiry.

events.title: What do we do with what we learned?
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: The incident is closed and our internal review is written. How we present it will decide whether anything actually changes.

events.title: Two programmes, one architecture team
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: Identity and segmentation both need my people this quarter. Running both properly is not possible. Running both badly is, and I would rather not.

events.title: A material risk the board has not seen
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: We are holding a material risk assessment the board has never been shown. Unless you take it there sooner, they will first hear of it in the next quarterly paper.

events.title: An observation from your SOC lead
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: Something I have noticed: we spend most of our time on the estate we can see, which is the estate that was built recently and properly. The parts I worry about are the parts we have no telemetry for, so they never appear on any of our reports.

events.title: The privileged vault covers a third of administrators
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: The vault was bought two years ago and deployed to about a third of administrators. Adoption stopped at the point the infrastructure team objected to session recording, and nobody pushed.

events.title: One credential, forty repositories
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: The build pipeline authenticates to production with a single long-lived credential shared across forty repositories. Anyone who can influence a build can reach production.

events.title: The jump servers sit on the corporate network
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: Production administration runs through jump servers that sit on the same network as staff laptops. A phished laptop and an administrative session are two steps apart, not ten.

events.title: Some legacy systems are not backed up at all
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: A sample showed 23 legacy systems outside the central backup schedule, including two that support despatch. The systems least able to defend themselves are also the least recoverable.

events.title: A quiet week
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: Nothing to escalate this week. It is the right time to do something you have been putting off.

variants.title: Nothing on fire
variants.body: Nothing needs you this week. If there is an enquiry you have been meaning to commission, or a risk you have been meaning to look at properly, this is the week for it.

variants.title: A week to think
variants.body: The inbox is quiet. Quiet weeks do not last, and they are worth spending on something that will matter in the next busy one.

variants.title: Quiet, for now
variants.body: Nothing to escalate. I would spend the time on the thing we both know we have not looked at yet.

events.title: The risk register has been rewritten
events.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
events.body: I have closed eleven inherited entries that described systems we no longer run, and rewritten the rest as scenarios rather than findings. It reads like a description of this business now.

effectsOnReveal.reason: The risk register now describes the business as it is.
